request.spec:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the claims as a CSV file: a header line person,number,date,amount,due,status,period
then one line per claim, people in list order and each person's claims oldest first, retired people
included whether shown or not, with the figures as the screen shows them (an empty number, period or
n/a as it is). Quoting and line ends as the people export.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export claims CSV" button that downloads the claims, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

The change is only in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The page already loads all the claims, so the server and stored data didn't need to change.

- **The button** (`data-testid="export-claims"`) sits next to the people export and downloads `claims.csv`.
- **The file** starts with `person,number,date,amount,due,status,period`, then has one line per claim:
  - people are in list order, with retired people included whether shown or not;
  - each person's claims are oldest first (the reverse of the screen's newest-first list).
- **The figures** are worked out the same way the claim rows work them out. That includes the due with its rounding and late charge, `n/a` when there is no rate, an empty number while a claim is a draft, and an empty period when its due-by date falls in no period.
- **Quoting and line ends** match the people export. I moved the download code into a shared `downloadCsv` helper, which both exports now use.

Claims with status DELETED are listed in the file too, because the screen still shows them.
